summary_for_children: Surah Ibrahim compares a good word to a good tree, and teaches that gratitude brings more blessings. It records Ibrahim's prayer for his family in a dry valley.
world_title: The Valley of the Good Tree
environment_concept: A good tree with deep roots and high branches (14:24), an uprooted tree lying loose (14:26), a dry valley (14:37) and a river with sailing boats (14:32).
architecture_and_scenery: A great tree on a hill, a dry valley with a well, rivers and ships below, sun and moon overhead.

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Prayer for a Peaceful City
story_library.children_narration: Prophet Ibrahim prayed to Allah for the safety of a special city. He asked that his family be guided toward worship and that people would have reasons to be grateful. The surah also compares a good word to a good tree. Its roots are strong, its branches reach high, and it gives fruit. Imagine a tree whose roots are firmly planted in the ground. Just as strong roots help a tree grow, sincere faith and good actions help a person grow in character.

world_idea.title: The Roots of Faith
world_idea.description: Explore an ancient sanctuary-inspired environment, then build a symbolic tree by connecting roots, branches, and fruit to examples of good words and actions. The growing tree is an interactive representation of the Quranic parable, not a literal tree from Ibrahim's life.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
